defense_in_depth_findings.title: Rehearsal coverage label undercounts committed release-document mutations
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: docs/architecture/reviews/evidence/f017-representative-ffn-composition-release-v2-rehearsal-v1.json reports release_binding_mutations=24 while the committed suite test_release_load_bearing_mutations_reject in scripts/research/tests/test_f017_representative_ffn_composition_single_use_release_v2.py enforces 25 release-document mutations; independent re-execution confirmed all 25 reject. Coverage is strictly better than the evidence label claims; no enforcement path reads this count (validator requires only result=PASS and real_ffn_compositions=0).
defense_in_depth_findings.required_action: None for v2 (the rehearsal is hash-bound into the reviewed release bytes; correcting it would require a byte change). Record the precise mutation census in any future rehearsal evidence.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Working-tree validator and terminalizer bytes are not hash-checked by the executing wrapper
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: scripts/research/f017_representative_ffn_composition_release_wrapper_v2.py validate_fixed_bindings checks authorization, arithmetic, reuse authorizations, executor, approval contract, supersession, v1 release, and v1 review, and validate_review_chain checks all bindings at reviewed_head; but the working-tree copies of the validator invoked at preflight and of the terminalizer are not byte-checked against the release bindings before use. Self-verification of the executing wrapper is inherently limited; execution-code-head discipline relies on the operator running the bound bytes, which the approval's execution_code_head and reviewed_head checks are designed to attest.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_action: In any future revision (append-only), add working-tree SHA-256 checks for the bound validator and terminalizer to validate_fixed_bindings.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Re-hash window between authorization validation and durable state recording
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: In wrapper v2 main --execute, authorize() validates release/approval bytes, then begin_attempt, begin_ffn, and write_receipt re-read and re-hash the release and approval files when recording durable state. A machine-local byte swap in that window would be recorded (mismatching the validated hashes and the go-token binding) but not re-validated at record time. The terminalizer re-checks release identity at reconcile (ATTEMPT_RELEASE, FFN_RELEASE), and an adversary with that write access could subvert the wrapper itself, so no additional authority is lost.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_action: Optionally hash release and approval bytes once at authorize() and thread those values into the durable records in a future revision.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Concurrent-attempt loser can exit via uncaught FileExistsError traceback instead of FAIL_CLOSED JSON
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: begin_attempt's os.mkdir is the exclusive-creation gate; a losing concurrent invocation raises FileExistsError, which is not in the wrapper __main__ except tuple (ReleaseError, FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, CalledProcessError), so the loser exits with a traceback rather than the FAIL_CLOSED JSON envelope. Independently re-executed the committed race test: exactly one winner, zero ffn-start, zero compute for the loser; fail-closed behavior and single-use accounting are unaffected, only the error surface is non-uniform.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_action: Optionally include FileExistsError in the fail-closed handler in a future revision.

statement: REPRESENTATIVE FFN COMPOSITION SINGLE-USE RELEASE V2 ACCEPTED FOR SEPARATE APPROVAL
